suspected_defect: (1) Outage read as fact: `search_papers` swallows every source failure and returns `[]` (search.py:244-262), so with all three sources down `verify_by_title_search` returns HALLUCINATED 0.7 (598-606) and the SKIPPED fallback (834) is unreachable for title-only entries; stage 22 then blocks export. (2) `integrity_score` is `1.0` when every entry is SKIPPED (98-104), so a total outage scores as perfect integrity. (3) Real DOIs registered outside Crossref and not under `10.48550/`/`10.5281/` get a final HALLUCINATED 0.9 from a Crossref 404 (376-389) with no fallthrough to title search. (4) Stage 22 catches any exception and proceeds without the gate (_export.py:1023-1027). (5) `verify_by_arxiv_id` and the DOI/OpenAlex layers use raw `urllib` and bypass the breakers and rate limiters (LT-3, LT-4, LT-8).

Any cached HALLUCINATED (including one from LT-1 defect 1) is permanent and short-circuits every later run with no TTL (`_SOURCE_TTL["citation_verify"]`, cache.py:32, is never read by verify.py). The key is the title only (538-539), so a later entry with the same title but a fake DOI/eprint inherits VERIFIED. `_read_cache` drops `matched_paper` (548-555), so on a cache hit `cr.matched_paper` is None and stage 23 retraction screening skips the entry (_citations.py:507-510). `_read_cache` does not catch `OSError`.

Only a 429 moves the breaker (`_cb_on_429`). A non-429 failure while HALF_OPEN (HTTP error 249-250, retries exhausted 262-263) leaves the state at `half_open`: the cooldown is not doubled, nothing re-opens it, and every later call is allowed. 5xx and network errors never count toward a trip. `_reset_circuit_breaker` is called by no `berb/` code, so state leaks across runs in a long-lived process (`berb serve`).

Transition table is complete for `search_arxiv`, but: the counter `_cb_consecutive_429s` counts every failure, not only 429; `get_paper_by_id` and `download_pdf` (224-276) ignore the breaker and never feed it; `_reset_circuit_breaker` is never called outside tests (state leaks across runs); with `raise_on_failure=False` a failure halfway through `client.results()` returns the partial `papers` list (221) as if complete.

The outage signal is lost at the boundary: the return type is `list[Paper]`, `failure_counter` is opt-in (`search_papers_multi_query` passes it, `verify_by_title_search` and `_citations.py:192` do not). All-sources-down with no cache returns `[]`, indistinguishable from "no such paper". On outage, stale cache (up to 3 days) is returned with no marker. `_cache_if_found` can raise `OSError` inside the `try`, which is then misclassified as a source failure and the cached rows are added on top of the already-extended results (214-215, 244-260).

(1) `screen_bibliography` skips `UNKNOWN` (206-207), so an unchecked reference leaves no finding. (2) `resolve_retraction` stores whatever `parse_retraction` returns (318), including an `UNKNOWN` produced by both fetches failing, for 30 days, and `cached_lookup` serves it back. A one-sided outage (Crossref down, OpenAlex `is_retracted:false`) is stored as `NONE` for 30 days (184-187). (3) The key is `cite_key`, not DOI (240, 253): a different paper using the same key in another run inherits the stored state. (4) Stage 23 only looks up entries with `matched_paper.doi`, which only the title-search layer fills, so DOI/OpenAlex/cache-hit results are never screened (_citations.py:505-510).

Outage looks novel: `search_papers_multi_query` swallows failures, so `total_papers_retrieved == 0`; with any `papers_already_seen` (the normal case, stage 4 candidates) the coverage is `"partial"`, not `"insufficient"` (390-393), the score is 1.0/`"high"` and the recommendation is `"proceed"`. The `"abort"` verdict gates nothing.

`real_search` is `bool(papers)` (469-470), so papers served from stale cache during an outage, or from the Perplexity top-up, count as a live search. The outage path is a LLM-generated-candidates fallback, which is the failure mode W3 targets. Cross-check with the pipeline-core reader.

A missing corpus is indistinguishable from "no tortured phrases": the stage skips screening silently (`_phrase_corpus.size` falsy, _literature.py:929) and writes no artifact. Advisory-only severity, low damage.

One lazily created client is shared by two different hosts: if `_mcp_call` creates it first (base_url `mcp_url`), the REST fallback `_list_collections_api` reuses it (`if self._http_client is None`) and sends the Zotero API path to the MCP server without the `Zotero-API-Key` header. Failures return `[]` (309, 395), so an outage reads as "no collections". `close()` leaves a closed client in place. Also `claude_scholar.py:57` calls `client.list_collections_sync()`, which no method in the file defines (unverified: possibly provided by a mixin I did not find).

Two writers of `current_cycle` agree mid-loop (set to N at :290, bumped to N+1 at :166) but leave N+1 after a normal exit and N after a `no_tasks_remaining` break; the loop never reads the restored value (`for cycle in range(1, ...)` :288), so a rerun over a restored model restarts numbering at 1 and duplicates `source_cycle` values, and a restored already-converged model still runs one full cycle before `converged()` is checked (:304).

`_slice_cost` sums `getattr(r, "cost_usd", 0.0)` over `StageResult`, which has no `cost_usd` field (`_helpers.py:74-83`), so every outcome costs 0.0 and `research.discovery.budget_usd` can never trip; also spend is not restored on a rerun and the cap is checked only after a whole cycle ran (overshoot up to width tasks).

An open question or contradiction is never closed: `converged()` stays False while any contradiction exists or a question has `priority > 0.7` (:240-244), and a question whose task produced a non-empty outcome is proposed again every cycle (only empty outcomes add a dead end, `discovery_loop.py:361-370`); `_cap_list` silently drops the oldest established findings and dead ends past 50, enabling re-exploration.

Verdict is encoded twice (enum field and list membership) and a third time as the stage-15 `decision` string (`proceed/pivot/refine` in `StageResult.decision`, upper-cased here); any non-`PROCEED` text, including an unexpected value like `"PROCEED "` (no strip, :302), becomes a REFUTED finding plus a new open question, which feeds RL-3's never-closing questions.

World model is saved only after the whole loop (`discovery.py:366-367`), so a crash mid-loop loses all epistemic state while `index.jsonl` keeps the crashed attempt's lines (never truncated) and `promote_best_task` may promote a slice the model never saw; and if the run fails in stage 16 before its checkpoint, resume restarts at stage 7 (checkpoint still at 6) and reruns the whole discovery loop, spending again.

A corrupt or non-list file reads as 0 (`:76-78`) so the pivot cap resets; `record_decision_history` then starts from `[]` and overwrites the remaining history (`:87-103`); the `attempt = pivot_count + 1` that results can collide with an existing `stage-NN_v1`, which `_version_rollback_stages` `rmtree`s (:148-149). Counts every entry, so "PIVOT/REFINE" mixing is by design.

Not atomic: a crash between `record_decision_history` and the loop (or mid-loop) leaves the cap consumed with some stages renamed and some not, and nothing rewinds `checkpoint.json` here; only stages rollback..15 are renamed, so stage 16+ output from the earlier pass stays in place and is read by the rerun (unverified for stages that do not overwrite).

When the best candidate is an older `stage-14_vN`, the current `stage-14/experiment_summary.json` and `charts/` are overwritten with no backup of the latest iteration (`:226-241`), so later `_consecutive_empty_metrics` (`:35-61`) compares an older iteration as "current" (unverified whether this masks empty metrics in practice).

`berb project list` can only ever show `[idle]`, because `berb run` never calls `start_run`/`finish_run`; a project left `running` by a crash would never be reset (no recovery), and `finish_run` accepts any string.

`_load_registry` catches `JSONDecodeError`/`KeyError` and leaves `projects` empty (`:43-44`), so the next `create`/`switch` rewrites the registry with only the new entry and the whole previous registry is lost; a crash during `write_text` truncates it the same way.
